newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suez drops on SocGen downgrade.
newsitem.headline: Suez drops on SocGen downgrade.

text.p: Shares in French holding company Cie de Suez fell more than three percent on Tuesday, after Societe Generale downgraded the stock to underperform from outperform.

Societe Generale analyst Pierre Flabbee said Suez stock, which has outperformed the CAC-40 index by 19 percent since September, had become expensive. "The cleaning up (of the accounts) and more openness (of the group), and even a possible merger with Lyonnaise des Eaux, seem to me priced into the share's outperformance since September," he said.
Suez was down 3.25 percent at 270.6 francs at 1103 GMT, on volume of 489,666 shares. The market was down 0.47 percent.
Another French broker said the rumoured merger with Lyonnaise was a "done deal" and the market was just waiting for the announcement.

The fall in stock prices reflected profit-taking on the Suez-Lyonnaise merger and the market wanted to know what the deal would lead to in terms of restructuring, with speculation of a merger between Suez's Belgian Tractebel unit, held through its SGB holding company, and Lyonnaise.
Analysts are talking about a share offer of two Suez shares for every one Lyonnaise share.
Lyonnaise was down 1.22 percent at 568 francs.
